subject: Token economics + batching assumptions — next steps and checklist

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Jan 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: token volumes + batching assumptions (recap + ask)

Lena — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can lock in an accurate cost estimate and propose an initial Dedicated sizing / autoscale profile.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary use: in-product summarization and long-form generation for power users. Typical prompt -> 700–1,200 tokens output, with a small (10–15%) proportion of much longer sessions (~3k tokens).
- Expected monthly volume (you mentioned a range): roughly 50M–200M tokens / month to start, with pilot targeting the low end and growth into the high end over Q2/Q3.
- Traffic pattern: mostly steady daytime usage across US regions with periodic peaks tied to nightly batch jobs and a small marketing-driven spike (~8–12 hours / month).

Asks for confirmation (so our price math matches your budget)
1) Can you confirm the tokens/month range you expect to commit for the pilot vs. production? Pilot (month 1–3) vs steady-state (month 4+).
2) Target cost goal: you mentioned wanting to be around $900 / 1M tokens (GROSS). Is that the correct target for the initial commit?
3) Concurrency / latency targets: what percent of calls need sub-300ms P95? Any hard latency SLO?

Our assumptions for the estimate we will build:
- Continuous batching enabled: we assume low-latency continuous batching will be applied to steady traffic to capture ~25–35% per-token improvement vs naive single-request execution.
- Typical concurrency for sizing: 50–150 concurrent requests during steady-state, spiking to 200–300 for short windows.
- Average request size for batching math: 800 tokens output + 50 tokens input = 850 tokens total.

Next steps / ask from you:
- Reply with the confirmed pilot vs production tokens/month and any hard latency SLOs.
- If you have an internal budget range for monthly spend (pilot & steady-state) that helps us map to tiered discounts.

Attachments: I’m attaching a sketch estimate (redwood-estimate-ACME.xlsx) and a short doc with the batching assumptions we’ll use (redwood-batching-assumptions.pdf).

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Post-demo: token volumes + batching assumptions (recap + ask)

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. Quick answers inline: 

- Pilot vs production tokens/month: Pilot (months 1–3): plan for 60M tokens/mo. Production (month 4+): planning for 160M tokens/mo if performance is stable and cost fits the budget.
- Cost target: yes — our procurement guideline is ~ $800–$1,000 / 1M tokens (gross) for standard usage. We can stretch for special price for high-volume committed tiers.
- Latency SLO: 90% of calls should be < 400ms, P95 < 700ms. Longer (> 1s) is acceptable for non-interactive batch outputs.

Concurrency: our internal telemetry suggests steady concurrent sessions ~60–120, with short peaks up to ~220 when we have a marketing push or nightly job. Average request size lines up with your 800–900 token estimate (we sampled 200 requests).

We’re good with continuous batching — we want to make sure it doesn’t push interactive latency over the SLO; if batching adds >200ms tail latency on critical calls, we’d prefer falling back to smaller batch sizes.

Happy to jump on a 30-minute call early next week to walk through the estimate.

—Lena

Lena — looping in Karthik (SE) and sending a short estimate and explicit batching/concurrency math so you have something concrete for procurement. See bullets below; the attached XLSX has the detailed tabs.

High-level unit-econ scenarios (assumptions)
- Baseline request size: 850 tokens (800 out + 50 in).
- Pilot (60M tokens / month): ~70k tokens/hour average (over 30 days) -> ~82 requests/sec equivalent if average request=850 tokens (60,000,000 / 30 / 3600 / (850/1) ≈ 82 rps).
- Steady-state (160M tokens / month): ~219 requests/sec equivalent (same math).

Batching effect estimates (continuous batching enabled)
- Continuous batching at steady traffic + 50–150 concurrent sessions: expected batching factor ~1.25–1.4 (i.e., 25–40% fewer GPU tokens billed after kernel-level amortization and shared KV handling).
- With quantized model variant (int8/4) + continuous batching + prefix caching for repeated prompts: estimated per-1M-token cost reductions:
  * conservative: $1,150 / 1M tokens -> with batching = $870 / 1M tokens (~24% savings)
  * expected: $1,050 / 1M tokens -> with batching = $700 / 1M tokens (~33% savings)
  * aggressive (high reuse + sustained batching): $950 / 1M tokens -> with batching = $600 / 1M tokens (~37% savings)

Latency vs batching tradeoffs (recommended guardrails)
- For critical interactive paths (P95 < 700ms target): cap batch size and use fast-path kernels; expected median increase from batching ~30–120ms depending on queueing window.
- For non-interactive / background jobs: use larger batching windows and allow up to 2–3s tail latency to maximize unit econ.

Sizing + autoscale recommendation (initial)
- Pilot: provision Dedicated pool sized for 1.5x expected steady concurrency (recommend 100 concurrent slots) with autoscale to 220 for peaks.
- Production: reserve capacity for 200 concurrent slots and autoscale to 400 during marketing spikes/nightly jobs.

Next steps / asks (action items)
- Acme: confirm pilot / prod tokens/month (you provided 60M / 160M — we’ll use that unless you change it).
- Redwood: we’ll deliver a formal pricing worksheet with the three unit-econ bands and a short SLO appendix (attached). Expect that doc by EOD today.
- Quick sync: propose Tue Jan 12, 09:00–09:30 PT for a 30-min call to walk numbers — does that work?

Attaching: redwood-estimate-ACME.xlsx (detailed pricing tabs) and redwood-batching-assumptions.pdf (assumptions & guardrails).

Thanks,
